The proposed solution concludes that $C = 1$, ignoring the explicit request to express $C$ in terms of the particle mass $m$ and the reduced Planck constant $\hbar$ ($x$). Dimensionally, since the Madelung–Bohm velocities $\pi_\mu$ and $u_\mu$ have units of velocity ($\text{length}/\text{time}$), their covariance has units of $\text{velocity}^2$, whereas the quantum Fisher information metric with respect to spatial translations has units of $1/\text{length}^2$. A non-trivial factor involving $m$ and $\hbar$ (specifically proportional to $m^2/\hbar^2$) is required for dimensional consistency, making $C = 1$ incorrect.

VERDICT: REJECT
